title: Set the boot Wi-Fi country on BCM4350/BCM43602 Macs
head: 0fbb7c6cbd10
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A live-ISO kernel command-line override can suppress the installed machine's drop-in
leads.consequence: When the installer ISO is booted with cfg80211.ieee80211_regdom=JP (for example to make its Wi-Fi usable), kmod in the target arch-chroot reports `options cfg80211 ieee80211_regdom=JP` from the ISO's /proc/cmdline. The new leaf treats that as an administrator's persisted target override and writes no /etc/modprobe.d/omarchy-brcmfmac-regdom.conf, even if the target's WIRELESS_REGDOM is US. The ISO computes target /etc/kernel/cmdline from the installed root configuration rather than copying the live ISO command line; after first reboot the early country hint is gone. Distinguish persistent modprobe files/target boot configuration from the running ISO's /proc/cmdline. Current test redirects -C to a fixture dir but does not model this chroot boundary.
leads.triage: confirmed by Opus follow-up (opus/followup-cmdline.md, review4 run) but unrealistic path (manual ISO boot-param edit, undocumented, outcome no worse than today); not published

leads.summary: Existing BCM4350/BCM43602 installations never receive the quirk on an update
leads.consequence: An installed Mac receives the new leaf as a packaged file, but `omarchy update` runs omarchy-migrate, not omarchy-apply-hardware. Without a migration, its /etc/modprobe.d/omarchy-brcmfmac-regdom.conf is never created or added to a later boot image; only a fresh install or a deliberate root rerun of `omarchy apply hardware` reaches this fix. The existing brcmfmac-supplicant repair has a migration explicitly because installation-only setup does not reach old machines. Add an idempotent migration for matching existing installs, consider rebuilding boot images and requesting a reboot; avoid claiming the update automatically fixes them.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F3); corroborated; published in More findings

leads.summary: Changing the saved regulatory country leaves the boot setting stale, even after rerunning hardware setup
leads.consequence: Fresh install with WIRELESS_REGDOM=US writes cfg80211=US. An administrator changes /etc/conf.d/wireless-regdom to GB and reruns hardware setup: the script sees its *own* US option through modprobe --showconfig and returns, leaving the file US, while wireless-regdb reads GB. It does not print a mismatch. A subsequent boot image can retain the stale country, especially when cfg80211 loads in initramfs before the root-side wireless-regdb udev helper. Treat the file this leaf owns separately from other administrators' overrides, update it on a changed valid country, and rebuild an already-created boot image if necessary. Extend the test: after the first run change WIRELESS_REGDOM to GB and assert the generated option changes to GB; the present test reruns only the same country.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F1 part); corroborated; published

leads.summary: The leaf brings back a full PCI config-space scan after #11259 removes it from hardware detection
leads.consequence: If related open PR #11259 merges as well, its sysfs-based `fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh` and other hardware leaves stop invoking lspci to avoid waking D3cold GPUs, but this new leaf still invokes `lspci -nn` on Apple hardware. pciutils reads configuration bytes for every PCI device, and the kernel may resume devices in D3cold for these reads. Thus each hardware rerun on an Apple system with a suspended PCI GPU reintroduces the scan that #11259 specifically removed. The files themselves do not overlap: #11259's diff does not change this new leaf or all.sh, so merging does not repair the call. Reuse its `omarchy-pci-id` helper or equivalent cached sysfs IDs if #11259 lands.
leads.triage: dropped: sibling leaf on quattro already uses lspci; #11259 unmerged; consistency only

limits: No physical Apple Broadcom hardware or actual new ISO install was run, so RF behavior and boot image content on a production Mac were not measured. Config-file behavior, kernel/kmod semantics, current-base merge and changed tests were checked independently with pinned sources and sandbox fixtures.

flags.claim: The new drop-in overrides any Wi-Fi country set after installation. / Later country overrides lose to the drop-in
flags.why: Only overrides in modprobe files sorting before omarchy-brcmfmac-regdom.conf lose (e.g. #9019's cfg80211.conf). A later-sorting file, a kernel cmdline cfg80211.ieee80211_regdom=, a runtime iw reg set, and the udev rule's iw reg set (if it runs) all win. The report scoped F1 to the PR's premise that the udev path is unreliable; the draft drops that condition.

flags.claim: Impact: the country cannot be changed without editing omarchy-brcmfmac-regdom.conf.
flags.why: Same alternatives as F-1, plus deleting the file. The report said: under the PR's premise, neither documented way (editing wireless-regdom, #9019's cfg80211.conf) works until someone edits the Omarchy file.

flags.claim: Suggested change: Name the drop-in so admin files sort after it, for example 00-omarchy-brcmfmac-regdom.conf.
flags.why: Line 9 states two defects; the rename addresses only the later-admin-file one. A changed WIRELESS_REGDOM stays stale after the rename because the leaf still treats its own file as an override. The report's suggestion also had: on rerun, rewrite Omarchy's own file from the current WIRELESS_REGDOM when no other override exists. The rename control only checked the admin-file case.

flags.claim: The leaf runs only on fresh installs
flags.why: It also runs on any manual rerun of omarchy-apply-hardware (usage: can be rerun later for diagnostics or after hardware/package updates); the draft's own line 9 relies on 'A rerun'. Correct part: nothing reruns it automatically and there is no migration.
Outside my evidence; the coordinator verifies with subagents and pi_job.py verify.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Later country overrides in earlier-sorting modprobe files, such as #9019's `cfg80211.conf`, lose to the new drop-in.

### Earlier-sorting overrides lose to the drop-in

modprobe orders options by file name and the kernel keeps the last `ieee80211_regdom=`, so #9019's `/etc/modprobe.d/cfg80211.conf` gives `ieee80211_regdom=GB ieee80211_regdom=US` and US wins. A rerun also ignores a changed `WIRELESS_REGDOM`, since the leaf treats its own file as an override. **Impact:** if the boot country comes from this option, as intended, editing neither `/etc/conf.d/wireless-regdom` nor `cfg80211.conf` changes it.

**Suggested change:** Name the drop-in so admin files sort after it (for example `00-omarchy-brcmfmac-regdom.conf`), and on rerun rewrite Omarchy's own file from the current `WIRELESS_REGDOM` if no other override exists.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 0fbb7c6)</summary>

Append this to `test/shell.d/brcmfmac-regdom-test.sh` (it reuses the file's `reset_fixture`, `run_setup`, `modprobe_dir` and `TEST_REAL_MODPROBE`):

```bash

# The kernel keeps the last ieee80211_regdom= that modprobe passes, and
# modprobe passes options in config file name order, as --showconfig lists them.
effective_regdom() {
  "$TEST_REAL_MODPROBE" -C "$modprobe_dir" --showconfig |
    grep -E '^options cfg80211 ' | grep -oE '\bieee80211_regdom=[^ ]+' |
    tail -n 1 | cut -d= -f2
}

# #9019's workaround, added after installation to pick another country.
reset_fixture
run_setup
printf 'options cfg80211 ieee80211_regdom=GB\n' >"$modprobe_dir/cfg80211.conf"
run_setup
[[ $(effective_regdom) == GB ]] ||
  fail "a country override added after installation takes effect" "effective: $(effective_regdom)"
pass "a country override added after installation takes effect"
```

Output at `0fbb7c6` (`bash test/shell.d/brcmfmac-regdom-test.sh`, exit status 1):

```
ok - country selection precedes the Apple boot quirk
ok - BCM4350 and all BCM43602 variants receive the boot country hint
ok - rerunning hardware setup is idempotent
ok - fresh installs derive their country from the target timezone
ok - older Apple vendor strings are recognized
ok - an explicitly configured country takes precedence over the timezone
ok - an existing country override in another modprobe file is preserved
ok - commented country overrides and unrelated options do not suppress the fix
ok - non-Apple hardware is unchanged
ok - wl-driven Macs, other adapters, and absent Wi-Fi do not receive the quirk
ok - a missing DMI vendor does not match Apple
ok - UTC, fixed offsets, and unknown timezones do not select an arbitrary country
ok - unset, world, and malformed country settings are not passed to cfg80211
ok - a missing regulatory configuration is left alone
ok - skipping the sourced quirk returns to its caller
effective: US
not ok - a country override added after installation takes effect
```

The same result on current `quattro` with the PR applied. With the drop-in renamed to `00-omarchy-brcmfmac-regdom.conf` (leaf and test `conf=` path), the whole file passes, including this case.
</details>

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

**Existing installs are not covered.**

The leaf runs only at install time or on a manual `omarchy-apply-hardware`, with no migration, so existing affected Macs are unchanged. **Suggested change:** add a migration, as `migrations/1786391100.sh` does for the sibling brcmfmac quirk, or state that the fix is install-only.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Open question (source analysis only, not reproduced):** the leaf acts only when `/etc/conf.d/wireless-regdom` already sets `WIRELESS_REGDOM`. wireless-regdb's own udev rule (`85-regulatory.rules`, running `set-wireless-regdom`, which does `iw reg set` with that value) runs `iw reg set` with that value each time `cfg80211` loads, and the module parameter ends in the same user regulatory hint. It is not clear whether the reporter's machine lacked a saved `WIRELESS_REGDOM`, in which case this leaf would not act either, or had one that the udev rule failed to apply. On an affected Mac with `WIRELESS_REGDOM="US"` saved and no `cfg80211` drop-in, a cold boot's `iw reg get` and `journalctl -b -k | grep -i regulatory` would show whether the existing path fails.

**Verified:**
- The PR test passes (15/15) at the head and on current `quattro` with the PR applied; mutants that drop validation, the override check or the vendor gate, or add `43a0`, fail it.
- `run_logged` sources the leaf in a child shell, so `return 0` ends only the leaf, and it runs after `set-wireless-regdom.sh`.
- The PCI IDs are BCM4350 and BCM43602 variants, a subset of `fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh`, with no overlap with `fix-bcm43xx.sh`.
- The override check ignores commented lines and covers other `modprobe.d` directories.

**Optional notes:**
- Without the `all.sh` line the test exits 1 with no output: the `grep -n` at line 87 fails under `set -euo pipefail` before `fail` can print. `|| true` there would give a readable failure.
- The `lspci` filler comment says it exposes `grep -q`/SIGPIPE under pipefail, but `run_logged` does not pass pipefail to the leaf; a `grep -q` mutant passes the whole file. Rewording the comment would avoid overstating that coverage.
</details>
